questions.question: Which of the following physical quantity measures the rate of work done?
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

__
 
• **Power (P)**: The rate of work done is called power.
 
• **Work done** is measured as the force on a body times the distance through which that force is applied.

Work done (W) = Force (F) x Distance (s).

**Power (P) = work done (W)/ Time taken.**

Energy (E) = power (P) x time (t).

Momentum (p) = mass (m) x velocity (v).

**EXPLANATION**__:

 
• The **force** is an interaction that changes the state of the rest of the state of motion of a body.
 
• The capacity of doing work is called **energy**.
 
• **The rate of work done is power.** So option 1 is correct.
 
• The product of mass and velocity is called **momentum**.

questions.question: A concave mirror produces two times magnified (enlarged) real image of an object placed at 20 cm in front of it. Where is the image located?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** - 40 cm.**

**Given:**

The magnification (M) is 2 (since it's enlarged), and the object distance dₒ​) is 20 cm, we can solve for the image distance ( dᵢ ).

**Formula used**

**M = dᵢ/dₒ**

Where:

**M is the magnification,**

**dᵢ ​is the image distance,**

**dₒ​ is the object distance.**

 

Calculation:

 

2 = - dᵢ/ 20 

dᵢ= - 20 × 2

dᵢ= - 40 

The** negative sign **indicates that the **image is formed on the same side as the object (i.e., it's a real image).**

**Therefore, the real image is located 40 cm in front of the mirror.**

questions.question: Which organ produce bile fluids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Liver__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__**Liver :**__

__
 
• The liver is the **largest internal organ** in the human body.
 
• It is located on the **upper right side** of the abdomen.
 
• It plays a crucial role in **metabolism, digestion, **and **detoxification**.
 
• It **produces bile** to **aid in digestion** and the** absorption of fats**.
 
• **Stores important nutrients** such as **vitamins** and **minerals**.
 
• **Filters and processes blood**, **removing toxins** and **waste products**.
 
• Regulates **blood sugar levels** by storing and releasing **glucose**.
 
• It can** regenerate itself** if damaged, but prolonged damage can lead to liver disease.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Organ**
 **Functions**
 
 

 **Kidney**
 
 
 
• The kidneys are** bean-shaped** organs located on **either side of the spine**, **below the rib cage**.
 
• Their main function is to **filter waste** and **excess fluids** from the** blood** to **form urine**.
 
• The kidneys also help **regulate blood pressure**, produce** red blood cells**, and maintain a** balance of electrolytes** in the body.
 
• Each kidney contains about a** million tiny filters **called** nephrons**, which help in the filtration process.
 
• Kidney disease can lead to a buildup of waste **and fluid** in the body, causing various health problems.
 
 
 
 

 **Tongue**
 
 
 
• The tongue is a** muscular organ** located in the** mouth**.
 
• It is covered with** tiny bumps** called **papillae**, which contain** taste buds** that help us perceive different tastes like **sweet, sour, salty, and bitter**.
 
• The tongue plays a crucial role in **chewing, swallowing, and speaking**.
 
• It is also involved in the process of **digestion**, as it helps **mix food with saliva** to form a **bolus** that can be easily swallowed.
 
• The tongue is **highly flexible** and can move in various directions, allowing us to manipulate food and produce different sounds while speaking.
 
 
 
 

 **Pancreas**
 
 
 
• The pancreas is a **long, flat gland** located **behind the stomach** in the **abdomen**.
 
• It plays a key role in **digestion** and in **regulating blood sugar levels**.
 
• The pancreas produces **digestive enzymes** that help break down food in the small intestine.
 
• It also produces** hormones**, including **insulin and glucagon**, which regulate blood sugar levels.
 
• **Insulin** helps** lower blood sugar levels** by allowing cells to take in glucose from the bloodstream, while **glucagon** helps **raise blood sugar levels** by releasing stored glucose into the bloodstream.
 
• **Dysfunction of the pancreas** can lead to conditions such as **diabetes**, **pancreatitis**, and **pancreatic cancer**.

questions.question: Which of the following are species of plants and animals which are found exclusively in a particular area?
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is ‘Endemic Species’**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Endemic species:**

 
 
• Endemic species are those plants and animals that are found **exclusively in a particular geographical area** and nowhere else in the world.
 
• They develop unique physical and biological characteristics due to long-term isolation and specific environmental conditions.
 
• Because of their limited distribution, endemic species are highly sensitive to habitat destruction, climate change, and human interference.
 
• **Examples:**
 
 
• The **Nilgiri tahr** is endemic to the Western Ghats of India.
 
• The **lion-tailed macaque** is found only in the tropical rainforests of the Western Ghats.
 
• The **Galápagos giant tortoise** is endemic to the Galápagos Islands.
 
• The **Kangaroo** is an endemic animal of Australia.
 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Evolutionary species:**

 
 
• Evolutionary species refer to organisms studied in terms of genetic change and evolution over time.
 
• This concept explains how species develop but does not imply restriction to a single geographical area.
 
 
 
• **Endangered species:**
 
 
• Endangered species are those that face a high risk of extinction due to declining population.
 
• They may exist in more than one region; for example, the tiger is endangered but not endemic.
 
 
 
• **Extinct species:**
 
 
• Extinct species are organisms that no longer exist anywhere on Earth.
 
• The dinosaur is a well-known example of an extinct species.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Endemic species are indicators of regional ecological uniqueness.
 
• Loss of endemic species leads to permanent biodiversity loss.
 
• Regions with a high number of endemic species are often declared biodiversity hotspots.
 
• Understanding endemic species is essential for conservation-based questions in competitive examinations.

questions.question:
A, B, C, and D represent four media as follows:

A- Hydrogen

B- Seawater

C- Copper 

D- Steel

 Which of the above media, spread the sound least and maximum respectively?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **A and D.**

__**Concept:**__

**Sound:**

Sound is a form of** energy** that travels through matter as waves, produced by vibrations. The properties of sound include:

 
• **Mechanical Wave:** Sound requires a medium to travel, such as air, water, or solids.
 
• **Longitudinal Waves: **Vibrations occur parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
 
• **Speed and Pitch:** The speed of sound depends on the medium's properties, while pitch is determined by frequency.
 
• **Amplitude and Loudness:** Amplitude affects the sound's loudness, with greater amplitude resulting in louder sounds.
 
• **Applications:** Sound is essential in communication, music, entertainment, navigation, and various industrial and scientific fields.

**Explanation:**

 
• The speed of sound is directly related to the density of the medium through which it travels. 
 
• The speed of sound varies depending on the medium through which it travels. The speed of sound is **fastest in solids, slower in liquids, and slowest in gases. Therefore, based on this principle:**
 
 
• The medium that would spread sound the** least would be D- Steel**, as sound travels **fastest** through solids, has a higher density and steel is a solid material.
 
• The medium that would spread sound the** most would be A- Hydrogen, **as sound travels **slowest** through gases, and has a lower density.
 
 

**So, among the given options, **hydrogen (A)** would spread sound the least, while **steel (D)** would spread sound the most.**

questions.question: Which of the following is difficult without friction?

options.text: Moving a heavy box from one place to another

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Holding a glass tumbler.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Friction between your fingers and the glass tumbler helps you to grip it and prevents it from slipping. 
 
• Without friction, the tumbler would be much harder to hold and would likely slip out of your hands.
 
• Friction:
 
 
• When a solid body slides over a stationary solid body, a force is exerted at the surface of contact by the stationary body on the moving body. This force is called the force of friction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/def261f2f67324b43ed5f4da5a1abfae79c2f804b90e0742bb3a26c787133322.png] 

 
• Laws of Dry Friction:
 
• The friction that exists between two surfaces which are not lubricated is known as dry friction.
 
• The following are the laws.
 
 
• The limiting frictional force is independent of the shape and area of the surface in contact.
 
• The force of friction acts in the opposite direction in which the surface is having a tendency to move.
 
• The frictional force acts tangentially to the contacting surfaces. 
 
• The force of friction is equal to the force applied to the surface, so long the surface is at rest.
 
• When the surface is on the point of motion, the force of friction is maximum and this maximum frictional force is called the limiting friction force.
 
• The limiting frictional force bears a constant ratio to the normal reaction between two surfaces.

questions.question:
Among the following statements, choose the correct statements.

A. Boiling point of alcohols increases with increase in the number of carbon atoms.

B. In alcohols, boiling points increases with increase of branching in carbon chain.

C. Boiling points of alcohols are lesser in comparison to haloalkanes of comparable molecular mass.

D. Boiling points of alcohols are higher in comparison to hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass.

E. The high boiling points of alcohols are mainly due to the presence of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
**__Explanation:-__**

 
• The boiling points of alcohols increase with increase in the number of carbon atoms (increase in van der Waals forces). In alcohols, the boiling points decrease with increase of branching in carbon chain (because of decrease in van der Waals forces with decrease in surface area)
 
• Boiling point of alcohols is more in comparison to hydrocarbons of comparable molecular mass due to intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
 
• Boiling point of alcohols are higher in comparison to other classes of compounds, namely hydrocarbons, ether, haloalkanes and haloarenes of comparable molecular masses.

**Note : **In statement E, we have to consider inter molecular hydrogen bonding instead of intramolecular hydrogen bonding.

questions.question:
Which of the following scenarios best demonstrates physical transformation?

1. Cutting a piece of wood into smaller pieces.

2. Burning a piece of paper to ash.

3. Mixing Baking soda and vinegar to produce carbon dioxide gas.

4. Digestion of food.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Cutting a piece of wood into smaller pieces.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **physical change **is a type of change that** alters the form or appearance of a substance** without changing its chemical composition. In other words, the substance remains the same chemically before and after the change. Physical changes involve changes in physical properties such as shape, size, texture, phase, or state of matter.
 
• Here are some common examples of physical changes:
 
 
• **Changes in State: **Changes from one state of matter to another, such as melting, freezing, vaporization (boiling or evaporation), condensation, or sublimation (solid to gas without passing through the liquid phase). For example, melting ice into water or freezing water into ice are physical changes.
 
• **Changes in Size or Shape:** Changes in the size or shape of an object without altering its chemical composition. For example, cutting a piece of paper, breaking a glass, or crushing a can are physical changes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e320b3b6dee1347c09620753cc2c1a298cd5e0613589a60f040a2e060cb30b7f.png] 

**Explanation:**__

 
• Cutting a piece of wood into smaller pieces is an example of a** physical change.** In this process, the wood is being physically altered in size and shape without changing its chemical composition. The wood remains the same substance before and after cutting; only its physical appearance and form have been modified. Therefore, cutting wood into smaller pieces is a reversible physical change.
 
• while others are chemical changes.

**Thus, Cutting a piece of wood into smaller pieces is an example of physical change.**
